newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs close up a hair in lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs close up a hair in lackluster trade.

text.p: Peruvian shares closed up a hair on Tuesday in lackluster trade, as investors await a possible hike in U.S. interest rates before deciding whether to enter the local market, brokers said.

The Lima Stock Exchange's General Index ended 0.01 percent higher at 1,662.13 points while the blue chip Selective Index rose 0.05 percent to close at 2,395.71 points. Turnover reached 27 million soles ($10 million), with 24 issues rising, 41 falling and 35 remaining flat. Brokers said a similar slow trading session is expected on Wednesday.
Analysts expect the U.S. Federal Reserve on March 25 will announce a slight hike in long-bond rates in order to iron out distortions in the U.S. economy.
"The issue of interest rates determines in these moments the behavior of regional bolsas," said jaime Jara of Inversion y Desarrollo brokerage.
"Investors have preferred to abstain to avoid surprises that affect their capital," he said, adding Wall Street's behavior often determines the trend in the local market.
Among the day's top gainers were power generator Edegel, which closed up 1.64 percent at 1.24 soles on trade of 332,957 shares.

Bolsa benchmark Telefonica del Peru, accounting for 25 percent of the day's trade, rose 1.19 percent to end at 5.97 soles on 1.15 million shares traded while brewer Compania Nacional de Cerveza rose 0.69 percent to 1.46 soles on trade of 626,467 shares.
Mining shares lost ground. Zinc-lead miner San Ignacio de Morococha fell 1.78 percent to 2.21 soles and miner Atacocha dropped 0.93 percent to 1.07 soles.
Leading Peruvian bank Banco de Credito closed down 0.45 percent to end at 4.40 soles.
"The market is responding well as it waits for the country's positive macroeconomic outlook to be fulfilled," said Israel Menor of Divisas y Valores brokerage.
"Shares have strong enough fundamentals to avoid entering a period of speculation," he added.
